explain.say: When a honeybee finds a good patch of flowers, she flies back to the hive and tells her sisters where it is with a dance. Karl von Frisch decoded this waggle dance and shared a Nobel Prize in 1973.

explain.say: On the upright comb she runs in a straight line, waggling her body, then loops round to repeat. The angle of that waggle run from straight up equals the angle of the food from the direction of the sun.

explain.say: The length of the waggle run gives the distance: the farther the flowers, the longer she waggles, very roughly a second of waggling for each kilometre, though the scale differs between bee populations.
Followers crowd round, feeling her movements in the dark and smelling the flower scent on her body. Then they fly out on the bearing she showed, adjusting as the sun moves across the sky.

faq.a: The waggle dance is how a honeybee forager tells her nestmates where food is. She runs straight while waggling her abdomen, loops back round one way, waggles again, loops the other way, tracing a figure of eight.

faq.q: How does the dance show direction?
faq.a: On the vertical comb, straight up stands for the direction of the sun. If the waggle run points 40 degrees to the right of straight up, the food lies 40 degrees to the right of the sun.
asks: How do bees use the sun in their dance?
What does the angle of the dance mean?

faq.q: How does the dance show distance?
faq.a: The longer the waggle run lasts, the farther away the food. Very roughly, each second of waggling stands for about a kilometre, but the exact scale varies between bee races.
asks: How do bees say how far away food is?
What does the length of the waggle mean?

faq.q: How can bees dance in a dark hive?
faq.a: Followers do not watch the dance; they feel it. They touch the dancer with their antennae, sense the vibrations and buzzing sounds, and smell the flowers on her body.
asks: Can bees see in the hive?
How do bees follow the dance?

faq.a: For flowers close to the hive, a bee does a quick circling dance that says food is nearby, so search around. Scientists now see it as a waggle dance with very short waggle runs.
asks: What does a bee circling dance mean?
How do bees show food that is close?

facts: Karl von Frisch shared the 1973 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine, partly for decoding the honeybee dance.
In the waggle dance, straight up on the comb stands for the direction of the sun.

quiz.say: A bee waggles straight down the comb. Where is the food?
quiz.show: A bee waggles straight down the comb. Where is the food?
quiz.why: Straight up means towards the sun, so straight down means the opposite direction.

wrong.1: Towards the sun would be a waggle straight up.
wrong.2: The dance points to food outside the hive.

quiz.say: A bee does a much longer waggle run than before. What has changed?
quiz.show: A bee does a much longer waggle run than before. What has changed?
quiz.why: A longer waggle run means a greater distance to the flowers.

wrong.1: Closer food gives a shorter waggle run.
wrong.2: The length tells distance, not the time of day.
